headline: The ethics panel believed the staffer. Gomez resigns.
summary: The House Ethics Committee said Monday it found substantial evidence that Rep. Jimmy Gomez, a California Democrat, made unwelcome sexual advances toward a House staffer, 'disregarding the power imbalance' between them. Gomez, 51, disagrees with the findings but will resign December 1. He had already lost his seat this month, by 25 points.

cover_question.q: Why does it matter he was the boss?

cover_answer: A boss holds your job. That makes no a risky word.
table_question: Can you say no to someone who's in charge of you?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A man who works in Congress, where the laws get made, is leaving his job early. A committee checked how he treated a woman who worked for him and said he broke the rules about how a boss treats people. It is like a coach who has to leave the team for breaking the rules. The grown-ups have handled it.
5-7.why: Only if they hear it. A boss broke the rules and is out: that is the whole shape, and it is enough.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, and nothing here is, so the script waits to be asked. The anchor is the coach who broke the rules and had to leave, a shape they know. Skip the kind of rule: one vivid detail becomes the whole thing at this age. Expect 'what did he do?' He was unkind to someone who worked for him.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Congress has an ethics committee, a referee for its own members. It spent months on a complaint that Jimmy Gomez of California made unwanted advances toward a woman on his staff. Monday it said the evidence was substantial, and being her boss made it worse. He quits December 1.
8-12.why: A referee for Congress: complaint, checking, ruling, consequence.
8-12.why_long: A ten-year-old is working out whether adults apply their own rules to themselves, and this story is that: Congress checking a congressman. The script runs the chain from complaint to resignation, so they see the referee works on a player already leaving. Expect 'was he punished?' No. The House ran out of time, and he quit first.

13-17.script: Does resigning count if you were leaving anyway? Jimmy Gomez lost his seat by 25 points, then an ethics panel found substantial evidence of unwelcome sexual advances toward a staffer he had power over. He disagrees, and quits December 1. Second: was the report itself the punishment?
13-17.why: He is going anyway, and the finding still landed. Which matters?
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: the resignation changes almost nothing, and the finding changed how he leaves. The second pair is a committee that ruled but could not punish, and a man who disagrees but goes. Expect 'why did she wait?' The incident was in 2024, the inquiry began in August, and the report does not say why.

5-7.a: No. Nobody has charged him with a crime. He broke Congress's rules, so he is leaving his job.

8-12.a: Members of both parties who check whether a congressman broke House rules.
He resigns December 1. He'd already lost his election.

13-17.q: Why does it matter he was the boss?
13-17.a: A staffer who says no to a boss risks her job. She left hers.

13-17.q: He says he disagrees. Could he be right?
13-17.a: He says it was consensual. The committee found substantial evidence it wasn't.
